title: Continuous-function condensation of topological modules
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative topological ring, and work on the coherent site of profinite sets in a fixed universe large enough for the coefficients [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. A topological $R$-module here is an $R$-module $M$ with continuous addition, negation and scalar multiplication $R\times M\to M$; morphisms are continuous $R$-linear maps. Use the sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. There is an additive functor $\mathscr C_R$ from these topological modules to internal $\underline R$-modules with the following specified formulas.

For every $M$, its underlying abelian sheaf is $S\mapsto C(S,M)$, with restrictions by precomposition and pointwise addition. Its action $\gamma_M:\underline R\otimes\mathscr C_R(M)\to\mathscr C_R(M)$ is the unique morphism whose restriction along the canonical map from the objectwise tensor presheaf sends $a\otimes h$ to $(s\mapsto a(s)h(s))$. This action satisfies the internal unit and associativity identities, so it is defined on the sheafified tensor, without an assertion that tensor-sheaf sections equal tensor products of sections.

For every continuous $R$-linear map $f:M\to N$, the underlying map of $\mathscr C_R(f)$ on $S$ is $h\mapsto f\circ h$; this is an internal $\underline R$-linear morphism. These maps preserve identities, composition and sums.

For every finite family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ with product topology, the canonical map
$$\mathscr C_R\left(\prod_{i\in I}M_i\right)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in I}\mathscr C_R(M_i)$$
is an internal module isomorphism, with section map $h\mapsto(\operatorname{pr}_i\circ h)_i$ and inverse $(h_i)_i\mapsto(s\mapsto(h_i(s))_i)$. For $M=R$ with its regular action, $\mathscr C_R(R)$ is the regular internal module over $\underline R$.

proof.text: Put $B(S)=C(S,R)$ as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-abelian-profinite-sheaf] to the additive topological group of each $M$, obtaining the abelian sheaf $P_M(S)=C(S,M)$. The natural pointwise tensor action $\beta_M$ of [lem-sfb-continuous-module-presheaf-coordinates] has the unit and associativity identities required for lifting. All these constructions have the same precomposition restrictions.

source.place: First two sentences; assembly from extracted lemmas, repair of original six-step proof

proof.text: Apply the first clause of [lem-sfb-section-action-internal] to the continuous commutative coefficient sheaf and the sheaf P_M from step 1. Its unital and associative hypotheses follow by evaluating beta on pure tensors and applying the sectionwise module laws from [lem-sfb-continuous-module-presheaf-coordinates]. Choose the uniquely normalized lift as the action of C_R(M). Naturality of the lax monoidal tensor comparison identifies the restrictions of the two internal linearity composites with the two presheaf composites; their equality is the action-commuting assertion of [lem-sfb-continuous-module-presheaf-coordinates]. Tensor restriction detects equality. Thus the unchanged postcomposition maps define an additive functor. The same restriction identity gives the pointwise action formula. For uniqueness, the displayed pointwise formula, the injectivity of the section coordinates and generation by pure tensors identify the restricted action with beta; tensor restriction then identifies the original sheaf action.

source.place: First two sentences; assembly from extracted lemmas, repair of original six-step proof

proof.text: Use the limiting finite-coordinate cone in presheaf modules supplied by [lem-sfb-continuous-module-presheaf-coordinates]. The forgetful functor to abelian presheaves preserves this limit. The sheaf inclusion reflects limits, and Mod.forget reflects limits by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates], so the same cone on the lifted objects is a product of internal modules. Its unique comparison with the chosen product is an isomorphism. Its composites with projections are the given images of continuous linear projections, so the forward section formula follows from the postcomposition formula. The inverse isomorphism followed by each original projection equals the chosen product projection; evaluating this equality gives the inverse section formula. The argument applies also to the empty finite index type.

source.place: First two sentences; assembly from extracted lemmas, repair of original six-step proof

proof.text: Use the regular presheaf-module isomorphism and its normalized section formula from [lem-sfb-continuous-module-presheaf-coordinates]. Forgetting to abelian presheaves makes it an isomorphism of the unchanged underlying sheaves. The chosen lifted action restricts to beta, and the prescribed coefficient multiplication restricts to pointwise multiplication by [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. Naturality of the tensor comparison and the presheaf regular action equation therefore show that this isomorphism is internal-linear. Its section formula is precisely the presheaf formula, giving the required regular normalization.

lean.note: The additive functor is existentially quantified together with natural additive section identifications with C(S,M). The action is characterized uniquely on canonical images of presheaf pure tensors; internal module laws are supplied by ModObj. Both finite-product section formulas and the regular-module normalization are explicit. The sole helper is the actual lax-monoidal tensor comparison applied to a pure tensor, with no postponed data.
